simple.meaning: קָרָה (qârâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “coolness.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 24:7. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָרָה (H7135) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: קָרָה (qârâh) / H7135 is traced through Job 24:7, Job 37:9, Psalms 147:17, Proverbs 25:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: They lie all night naked without clothing,

timeline.evidenceText: They lie all night naked without clothing,
Out of its room comes the storm,
He hurls down his hail like pebbles.
As one who takes away a garment in cold weather,

Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.

definitions.full: H7135. qarah קָרָה cold , see קרר קָרָה noun feminine id.; — absolute ק ׳בְּיוֺם Nahum 3:17 a day of coldness , cold day, so Prov 25:20 ; ׳ק alone, cold of night Job 24:7 ; in General, due to winds 37:9 ( מִמְּזָרִים see זרה Pi`el ; yet Voigt Bu, attractively , מִמְּזָוִים (compare Psa 144:13 ) out of storehouses [|| חֶדֶר ]); יַעֲמֹד מִי קָרָתוֺ לִפְנֵי 147:17 , + plural Zech 14:6 (read וְקָרוֺת , see יָקָר ).
